game.board_hint: by points ratio — so short and long periods stay comparable
game.footnote: Only days that are already over are counted. A zero day at the weekend counts half, because card and direct-debit bookings only arrive on the next banking day — an empty Sunday is often just a booking gap. For the same reason the most recent day can still rise.
game.rule: How points work: a day without spending scores 10 (5 at the weekend), below a quarter of the benchmark 6, below half 4, up to the benchmark 2. The benchmark is the median day with spending in this period. On top of that comes the month result: if something is left over, you get up to 20 % bonus points — full from 30 % of income.

settings.bridge.hint_linux: Linux: the download is a .zip — extract it, then double-click the extracted .sh (or run it from a terminal). Ollama is installed with the official curl | sh after a yes/no prompt.
settings.bridge.hint_mac: macOS: the download is a .zip — double-click it once to extract the .command file (the zip preserves the executable bit; without it browsers strip the bit and macOS refuses with “you don’t have permission”). Then double-click the extracted .command. The first launch may say the file “cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer” → right-click → Open → Open. Python 3 ships with modern macOS; Ollama is installed via Homebrew.
settings.bridge.hint_windows: Windows: double-click the .bat directly — nothing to extract. SmartScreen may say “Windows protected your PC” → “More info” → “Run anyway”. Needs Python 3 from python.org or the Microsoft Store. Ollama is installed via winget.

settings.ts.heading: On your phone, from anywhere (Tailscale)
settings.ts.not_served_hint: DocuSort is logged in to the tailnet, but nothing is published on port 443. Until that changes the address leads nowhere — and there is no fallback over the 100.x address.
settings.ts.phone_hint: Open this on the phone and add it to the home screen — then it looks like an app.
settings.ts.step_dns: There, under DNS, switch on MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates.
settings.ts.step_key: In the Tailscale console, under Auth keys, press “Generate auth key…” and switch on “Reusable”. Not the button below it (“Generate access token…”) — that one is for something else. The right key starts with tskey-auth-.
settings.ts.step_paste: Paste the key here and press Connect.
settings.ts.subtitle: Reach DocuSort over a private network — no port forwarding, nothing put on the internet. You need a free Tailscale account and one key, once.
settings.ts.unavailable: This image does not carry Tailscale yet. Take the update and a field will appear here.
settings.web.heading: Web server
settings.web.hint: Host: 0.0.0.0 = all interfaces. Port: 9876 by default — 8080 is already taken on a lot of machines (a NAS, a development box). Privileged ports < 1024 are not available — DocuSort does not run as root.
settings.web.https_active: HTTPS is active (TLS cert configured in config.yaml).
settings.web.restart_hint: Host or port changes take effect after the service restarts — you'll need to reach the UI at the new address afterwards.
settings.web.subtitle: Address and port the UI listens on.

spend.special_help: These categories count nowhere — neither in monthly spending nor in the fixed costs. The bookings stay visible and are shown separately.
spend.special_switch: Switch: count special pots in or leave them out
spend.special_title: What comes out of a special pot?
spending.accounts_budget_note: The budget alarm always covers all accounts and is hidden while a selection is active.
spending.accounts_hint: Applies to every figure on this page — spending, income, daily chart, game and leaderboard.
spending.click_hint: Click a category to see its bookings — change the category right there; DocuSort remembers it for that payee.
spending.empty_hint: For monthly spending, first import your bank statements as CSV under Finance. Bookings are then sorted automatically into buckets like Groceries, Drugstore or Amazon.
spending.footnote: Counts debits on spending accounts by their booking category. Transfers between your own accounts, savings accounts and saving categories (investments, savings insurance) are excluded — that money isn't gone. Pending transactions count only once the bank books them.
spending.learn_hint: Ticked, DocuSort remembers the assignment for this payee and applies it to its other bookings. Unticked, only this one booking changes.
spending.mode_hint: Switch between salary month (salary to salary) and calendar month
spending.new_fixed: Is “{label}” a fixed cost? (OK = yes, Cancel = no)
spending.new_saving: Is “{label}” saving/investment (money not gone, just elsewhere)? (OK = yes, Cancel = no)
spending.no_month_hint: There are no expense bookings for {month}. Pick another month above.
spending.open_hint: {n} bookings still without a category (Other) — assign them in the explorer
spending.pdf_hint: This period as a PDF — everything on one page
spending.range_salary: salary to salary (same as the budget alarm)
spending.subtitle: What came in and what it went on in the month — by the categories of your bookings, netted. Whatever you re-sort here or in the explorer counts immediately.

tx.ai_done: AI suggestions applied — marked “AI”, always overridable.
tx.ai_hint: The local AI suggests a category for every open payee (marked “AI”, always overridable).
tx.amount_hint: Amount without a sign — applies to money in and out
tx.anchor_saved: Start of month set to the {d} — salary months recalculated.
tx.assign_all2: bookings of that payee (future imports too) — DocuSort remembers the rule.
tx.by_hand: set by hand for exactly this booking
tx.card_note: Some banks first post card payments as a collective entry with a terminal number; the merchant name only arrives with the next statement.
tx.counts_fixed_short: counts as a fixed item on /fixkosten
tx.counts_saved_short: counts as saved/invested, not as spending
tx.delete_cat: Delete category — its bookings fall back to Other
tx.delete_cat_q: — delete it? Its bookings fall back to “Other” and its rules are removed.
tx.delete_rule: Delete rule — bookings fall back to the built-in detection
tx.fall_back: booking(s) fall back to the detection.
tx.fixed_q: ” as a fixed cost? (OK = yes, Cancel = no)
tx.intro2: period, amounts — all live. The totals above are exactly the list below (transfers between your own accounts are shown but not counted). Every booking carries a badge saying why it sits in its category.
tx.learn_hint: When you assign a category, DocuSort remembers the payee (IBAN and name) and files its other bookings along with it.
tx.learn_toggle: Learn the assignment for this payee
tx.learned_amount: learned only at {amt} → {cat} (this payee has several amount classes):
tx.new_cat_ph: New category, e.g. dog, garden, hobby electronics
tx.no_custom_cats: None of your own yet — the built-in ones often suffice; add what you miss.
tx.no_payee_learn: Without a payee name there is nothing to learn — please assign the bookings below one by one.
tx.no_reason: no reasoning stored — “run detection again” fills it in
tx.no_reason_long: No reasoning stored. “Run detection again” fills it in for all bookings.
tx.nothing_for_ai: Nothing open — the AI has nothing to do.
tx.nothing_open_cat: Nothing left open in this category. 🎉
tx.on_savings_account: · on a savings account (counts as saved/withdrawn)
tx.pending_hint: “Pending”. Name, date and amount can still change when the bank books them — that is why they stay out here and enter no total, no salary month and no fixed costs. With the next export in which they are booked, they disappear from here and appear below as a normal booking with the merchant's name.
tx.pending_n: transactions the bank has not booked yet
tx.rank_hint: Order of precedence: manual › transfer (IBAN) › learned rule › AI suggestion › built-in detection › the bank's booking type.
tx.rank_order: Order of precedence: by hand › transfer (IBAN) › learned rule › AI suggestion › built-in detection
tx.rerun_hint: Run the built-in detection and the learned rules over all bookings again (manual assignments and transfers stay).
tx.salary_month_hint: A month runs from salary to salary. If no salary is found in a month, it starts on this day.
tx.saving_cat_hint: Spending in this category counts as saved/invested, not as spent
tx.saving_hint: Savings plans, funds, life and pension insurance — money that is not gone, just elsewhere. Not counted as spending.
tx.saving_q: ” as saving/investment (money not gone, just elsewhere)? (OK = yes, Cancel = no)
tx.set_day_hint: Sets From and To to this day — shows all bookings of that day.
tx.special_done: {n} booking(s) now count as special expenses.
tx.special_hint: Money that really left the account but comes out of its own pot (house build, inheritance). Stays in the list, counts in no spending, monthly or fixed-cost figure.

tx.transfers_hint: Money between your own accounts — listed, but counted neither as income nor as spending.

update.docker_hint: Running in a container — here you replace the image, not the files:
update.docker_warn_second: Run this in the folder that holds your docker-compose.yml. 🔴 Never create a new container in your NAS interface instead — that updates nothing, it puts a SECOND DocuSort beside the first. Both want the same port and keep separate data: you set up one and open the other.

upload.background_hint: Uploading in the background — you can close this tab.
upload.csv_hint: Bank statements (PDF) and bank exports (CSV) belong here like any other document — they land in the library and in the finances at the same time. A CSV without its own IBAN (N26, comdirect) asks for the account right here.
upload.csv_needs_admin: This file names no account — please have an administrator import it
upload.csv_needs_iban: CSV without its own IBAN — please import it under Finances using the “Account IBAN” field
upload.drop_label_hint: PDF, JPG, PNG, TIFF, CSV · multiple files possible
upload.folder_picker_hint: Including subfolders — PDFs, images and bank CSVs mixed; anything unsupported is listed as skipped
upload.foreground_hint: Uploading — keep this tab open until the bar finishes. Already-uploaded documents continue to be classified on the server even if you close the tab.
upload.ocr_hint: OCR + Claude take 15–60 s per PDF depending on page count. The watcher waits 5 s after the last byte before it starts — see live status above.
upload.subtitle: The one place for everything: documents, receipts, bank statements (PDF) and bank exports (CSV) — single files, whole folders, drag & drop or a phone scan. DocuSort decides what belongs in the library and what belongs in the finances.
